messages:
mira: Heads-up — our /v1/generate docs show `inputs: []` in examples but OpenAPI schema says `inputs: object`. This is causing SDK codegen mismatch.
ryan: ugh, saw that in a bug report. Which page?
mira: https://docs.redwood.ai/api/generate — look at example under 'batching' — it's an array.
sam: can we change schema to accept array? or change examples to object?
alex: prefer keeping schema as object (single input) and add a separate `batch` example. Changing schema will break older SDKs.
jen: PR incoming — I'll update examples + add migration note. cc @ryan for approval.
jen: created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4234 — updates examples, adds note and unit test.
ryan: pinging eng-ml to confirm runtime accepts array vs object
eng-ml-bot: /cc @kai @lee - runtime currently accepts both but codegen expects object
kai: runtime handles lists but SDK wrapper flattens to single input; agree with not changing schema.
mira: ok let's update examples to object, and add a separate 'batching' example that shows array payload and notes about server fallback
sam: also update python snippet in SDK section — people copy-paste `client.generate(inputs=[...])` which will fail
jen: will add code samples: curl, python, ts with both single and batch. Also add note about migration: older clients may send arrays, we have fallback but recommend explicit batch param
ryan: Can we add an e2e test? maybe a small curl check in docs CI
jen: added docs test that fetches example and validates against openapi. See PR diff.
alex: 👍 I'll review today.
mira: thx. Quick ask — update model response schema example: `outputs` is currently string, but multi-output models send array. Need consistent example
jen: will add both single-output and multi-output samples and clarify schema is oneOf string|array
sam: lgtm
ryan: approving once CI green :thumbsup:
jen: thanks, merging after CI
